title: Erdős Problem #287 — Gaps in Egyptian Fraction Representations of One
statement:
For every integer $k\geq 2$ and every strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers $1<s(0)<\cdots<s(k-1)$ satisfying $\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\frac{1}{s(i)}=1$, the maximum consecutive gap
$$\max_{0\leq i<k-1}\bigl(s(i+1)-s(i)\bigr)$$
is at least $3$.

title: Erdős Problem #1025 — Independent sets for functions on pairs
statement: For every pair of distinct elements $x_i,x_j$ of an $n$-element set, choose $p(x_i,x_j)$ different from both. Call a subset independent if it never contains $x_i,x_j$, and $p(x_i,x_j)$ together. If $g(n)$ is the minimum, over all such functions $p$, of the largest independent-subset size, determine the order of $g(n)$. In particular, improve $c_1n^{1/3}<g(n)<c_2√(n log n)$.

title: Bollobás–Komlós bandwidth conjecture
statement: For every $\gamma>0$ and all $r,\Delta\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist $\alpha>0$ and $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every graph $G$ of order $n\ge n_0$ with minimum degree at least $(1-1/r+\gamma)n$ contains a copy of every graph $H$ of order $n$ whose chromatic number is at most $r$, whose maximum degree is at most $\Delta$, and whose band-width is at most $\alpha n$. Here, the band-width of $H$ is the smallest integer $k$ for which its vertices can be enumerated as $v_1,\ldots,v_{|H|}$ so that every edge $v_iv_j\in E(H)$ satisfies $|i-j|\le k$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/01](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/711), page 42. Canonicalized from 8 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Polynomial interpolation on the sphere: characterization of fundamental systems
statement: Let $S^2:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^3:\lvert x\rvert=1\}$, let $V_n$ be the space of spherical polynomials of degree at most $n$, and set $N:=(n+1)^2=\dim V_n$. Given $N$ pairwise distinct nodes $\{\xi_i\}_{i=1}^N\subset S^2$ and real data $\{y_i\}_{i=1}^N$, determine conditions on the node set such that there is a unique $P\in V_n$ satisfying $P(\xi_i)=y_i$ for every $i=1,\ldots,N$ (equivalently, such that the associated interpolation system is nonsingular).
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/27](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/710), page 39. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Hardness of Approximating Maximum Subgraphs with Hereditary Properties
statement: For every nontrivial hereditary graph property $\pi$ and every $\epsilon>0$, the maximum-subgraph-with-property-$\pi$ problem—given a graph $G$, find a maximum vertex-induced subgraph of $G$ satisfying $\pi$—cannot be approximated within a factor of $n^{1-\epsilon}$, unless $\mathrm{NP}=\mathrm{ZPP}$. Here, nontrivial means that $\pi$ holds for infinitely many graphs and fails for infinitely many graphs, and hereditary means that every vertex-induced subgraph of a graph satisfying $\pi$ also satisfies $\pi$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/28](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/730), page 29. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: PTAS claim for the ε-dense Group Steiner Tree Problem
statement: For every fixed $\\varepsilon>0$, the $\\varepsilon$-dense Group Steiner Tree Problem on unweighted graphs admits a polynomial-time approximation scheme. Here an instance consists of a graph $G=(V,E)$ with pairwise disjoint groups $S_1,\\ldots,S_m\\subseteq V$, and the objective is to find a minimum-edge tree containing at least one vertex from each group. Writing $S=\\bigcup_i S_i$, the instance is $\\varepsilon$-dense when $|N_{V\\setminus S}(S_i)|\\geq \\varepsilon |V\\setminus S|$ for every $i$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/28](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/730), page 36. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Rapid mixing of Glauber dynamics for proper graph colorings
statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $\Omega$ be the set of proper $k$-colorings of $G$. The Glauber dynamics updates a uniformly chosen vertex by assigning it a uniformly chosen color not used by its neighbors, leaving all other colors unchanged. The report conjectures that, whenever $k\geq \u0000Delta+2$, this chain converges rapidly to the uniform stationary distribution on $\Omega$; in particular, the $O\!\left(n\log(n/\u0000epsilon)\right)$ convergence bound stated there for $k>2\u0000Delta$ should hold throughout the range $k\geq \u0000Delta+2$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/28](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/730), page 39. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Linear-time approximation for the weighted matching problem
statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph with edge-weight function $w:E\to\mathbb{R}_+$. A matching is a subset $M\subseteq E$ such that no two edges in $M$ are incident to the same vertex, and its weight is $w(M):=\sum_{e\in M}w(e)$. For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a linear-time approximation algorithm for the maximum-weight matching problem whose performance ratio is $\frac{2}{3}-\varepsilon$; that is, on every such graph it returns a matching of weight at least $(\frac{2}{3}-\varepsilon)$ times the weight of an optimal matching.

title: Kato square root problem for divergence-form operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$
statement:
Let $H_1=L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $H_2=L^2(\mathbb{R}^n;\mathbb{C}^n)$, $V=W^1_2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $S=\nabla$, and let $A=(a_{jk})\in L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n;\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{C}^n))$ satisfy the accretivity condition inherited from the preceding formulation. For the associated divergence-form operator $L=-\operatorname{div}A\nabla$, determine whether
\[
D(\sqrt{L})=V
\quad\text{and}\quad
\|\sqrt{L}u\|\approx\|\nabla u\|
\]
for all $u\in V$.

title:
Polynomial-time computation of the mod-
\(\ell\) Galois representation attached to \(\Delta\)
statement:
Let \(\ell\) be prime, and let \(V_{\ell}\) be the two-dimensional mod-\(\ell\) Galois representation associated with the level-one, weight-12 modular form
\[
\Delta=q\prod_{n\ge 1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge 1}\tau(n)q^n.
\]
Assume that the image of the Galois group contains \(\operatorname{SL}(V_{\ell})\) (excluding only finitely many \(\ell\)). Show that \(V_{\ell}\) can be computed in time polynomial in \(\ell\), where “computing \(V_{\ell}\)” means producing the minimum polynomial over \(\mathbb{Q}\) of a generator of the finite Galois extension \(K_{\ell}\) whose Galois group is the image of the representation on \(V_{\ell}\).

title: Joint universality conjecture for orthogonal families of Selberg-class $L$-functions
statement:
Suppose that $L_1,
obreak\ldots,L_m$ are elements of $\widetilde{\mathcal S}$ satisfying
$$
\sum_{p\le x}\frac{a_{L_j}(p)\,\overline{a_{L_k}(p)}}{p}
=\delta_{jk}\,\kappa_j\log\log x+O(1),
$$
where $\kappa_j>0$ and $\delta_{jk}=1$ if $j=k$ and $\delta_{jk}=0$ otherwise. For $1\le j\le m$, let $g_j$ be continuous on $K_j$ and non-vanishing in the interior, where each $K_j$ is a compact subset of
$$
D=\left\{s:\max\left\{\frac12,1-\frac1d\right\}<\operatorname{Re}s<1\right\}
$$
with connected complement, and $d$ is the maximum of the degrees of the $L_j$. Then, for every $\varepsilon>0$,
$$
\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac1T\operatorname{meas}\left\{\tau\in[0,T]:\max_{1\le j\le m}\max_{s\in K_j}\left|L_j(s+i\tau)-g_j(s)\right|<\varepsilon\right\}>0.
$$
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2004/46](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/760), page 54. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Quasioptimal finite-element error estimates for Willmore flow of graphs
statement:
Suppose that the problem (2)–(4) has a smooth solution on the interval $[0,T]$. Then
$$
\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|(u-u_h,w-w_h)(t)\|+\left(\int_0^T\|u_t-u_{ht}\|^2\,dt\right)^{1/2}\c7h^2|\log h|^2,
$$
and
$$
\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|\nabla(u-u_h)(t)\|+\left(\int_0^T\|\nabla(w-w_h)\|^2\,dt\right)^{1/2}\ch.
$$
Here $(u_h,w_h)$ is the semidiscrete finite-element solution defined on page 17, and $h$ is the maximum mesh size.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/10](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/791), page 16. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Interpolation on a smooth manifold with prescribed points and endpoint velocities
statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-dimensional manifold embedded into $\\mathbb{R}^N$ so that, for every $p\in M$, the tangent space $T_pM$ can be considered as an affine subspace of $\mathbb{R}^N$. Find a $C^2$-smooth curve $\gamma:[0,\tau]\to M$ satisfying
\[
\gamma(t_i)=p_i\quad (1\le i\le k-1),
\]
for a given set of distinct points $p_i\in M$ and fixed times
\[
0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_{k-1}<t_k=\tau,
\]
and, in addition,
\[
\gamma(0)=p_0,\qquad \gamma(\tau)=p_k,\qquad \dot\gamma(0)=\xi_0\in T_{p_0}M,\qquad \dot\gamma(\tau)=\xi_k\in T_{p_k}M,
\]
where $\xi_0$ and $\xi_k$ are given tangent vectors to $M$ at $p_0$ and $p_k$, respectively.

title: Nonlinear output regulation via nonlinear internal models
statement:
For the nonlinear system
\[
\dot z=f_0(w,z)+f_1(w,z,e)e,\qquad
\dot e=q_0(w,z)+q_1(w,z,e)e+u,
\]
with exosystem \(\dot w=s(w)\), compact admissible initial-condition sets \(W,Z,E\), and Assumptions 1 and 2 of the report, construct an internal-model controller
\[
\dot\eta=\varphi(\eta)+Gv,\qquad u=\gamma(\eta)+v,
\]
so that, for sufficiently large \(\kappa\), the additional choice \(v=-\kappa e\) makes the closed-loop positive orbit bounded and ensures \(e(t)\to0\) as \(t\to\infty\), uniformly over the admissible initial conditions. The report describes this construction using a high-gain observer, with \(\varphi\), \(G\), and \(\gamma\) chosen from the locally Lipschitz function \(f\) in Assumption 2.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/11](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/792), page 29. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Exact determination of Tverberg’s separation number
statement: For each positive integer $k$, determine the minimal positive integer $s(k)$ such that every collection of at least $s(k)$ nonempty convex sets in the plane with pairwise disjoint relative interiors admits a $(1,k)$-separation: a closed half-plane containing at least one of the sets, while the complementary closed half-plane contains at least $k$ of the remaining sets. The report records the bounds $3k-1\le s(k)\le 12(k-1)$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/17](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/822), page 30. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Optimal-complexity realization of the adaptive refinement condition
statement:
For hierarchical refinement of a tree of admissible meshes, let \(V_N=\{V\text{ admissible}:\dim(V)=N\}\), and let \(\phi:\bigcup_{N\in\mathbb N}V_N\to\mathbb R\) be a quasi-monotone error measure satisfying
\[
V\subset\widetilde V\ \Longrightarrow\ \phi(V)\le c_\phi\phi(\widetilde V).
\]
For \(\varepsilon>0\), define \(V_\varepsilon=\{V\text{ admissible}:\phi(V)\le\varepsilon\}\), and assume
\[
\sup_{\varepsilon>0}\varepsilon^{-1/s}\inf_{V\in V_\varepsilon}\dim(V)<+\infty
\]
for some \(s\ge0\). Can a refinement algorithm construct spaces \(V_k\) satisfying, for some constant \(\rho<1\),
\[
\widehat V_k=\{V\supset V_{k-1}:\phi(V)\le\rho^k\phi(V_1)\},\qquad \dim(V_k)\le\dim(V)\quad\text{for every }V\in\widehat V_k,
\]
with optimal complexity?
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/37](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1058), page 10. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Efficient computation of earliest-arrival transshipments with multiple sources and one sink
statement: Given a network with arc capacities $u_e\ge 0$ and transit times $\tau_e\ge 0$, multiple source nodes with prescribed positive supplies, and a single sink with the corresponding demand, compute a flow over time with the earliest-arrival property: for every time horizon $\theta\ge 0$, the amount of flow that has reached the sink by time $\theta$ is maximal among feasible flows satisfying the transshipment requirements. The report asks for an efficient algorithm for this problem, specifically one whose running time is polynomial in the input size plus the number of breakpoints of the earliest-arrival pattern and that does not use time-expanded networks.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2005/50](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1111), page 39. Canonicalized from 6 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Additive approximation of monotone edge-deletion problems
statement: Let $\mathcal P$ be a monotone graph property, and let $E'_{\mathcal P}(G)$ be the minimum number of edge deletions needed to transform a graph $G$ into a graph satisfying $\mathcal P$. Characterize those monotone properties for which, for some $\delta>0$, $E'_{\mathcal P}(G)$ can be approximated in polynomial time to within additive error $n^{2-\delta}$ on $n$-vertex graphs. The report gives the following resolution: if some bipartite graph fails to satisfy $\mathcal P$, then such a $\delta>0$ and a polynomial-time approximation exist; if every bipartite graph satisfies $\mathcal P$, then for every $\delta>0$ it is NP-hard to obtain an additive-$n^{2-\delta}$ approximation.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2006/01](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1183), page 13. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Completion of an elementary hexahedron for a discrete conjugate net
statement: For a discrete conjugate net with $m=3$, given seven points $f$, $f_i$, and $f_{ij}$ such that the quadrilaterals $(f,f_i,f_{ij},f_j)$ are planar, find the eighth point $f_{123}$ so that the quadrilaterals $(f_i,f_{ij},f_{123},f_{ik})$ are planar as well. The report states that this problem has a unique solution generically, because the relevant planes in three-dimensional space intersect in exactly one point.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2006/12](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1194), page 6. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Negative convergence of stretch lines to Thurston’s boundary
statement: For every complete geodesic lamination $\mu$ on $\Sigma$ with non-empty stump $\gamma$, and every $g\in\mathcal T(\Sigma)$, determine whether the associated stretch line $t\mapsto g_t^\mu$ converges in the negative direction, $\lim_{t\to-\infty}g_t^\mu\in\mathop{\rm PL}_0(\Sigma)$, and identify the limit when it exists. The report establishes this when $\gamma$ is uniquely ergodic, in which case the limit is $[\gamma]$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2006/26](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1275), page 34. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Instance optimality in compressed sensing for a general norm
statement:
Given a norm \(\|\cdot\|_X\) on \(\mathbb{R}^N\) and \(k<N\), determine the minimal value of \(n\) for which there exists an encoding–decoding pair \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}^N\to\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\Delta:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^N\) such that
\[
\|x-\Delta(\Phi x)\|_X\le C_0\,\sigma_k(x)_X\qquad\text{for all }x\in\mathbb{R}^N,
\]
where \(C_0\) is independent of \(k\) and \(N\), \(\Sigma_k:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^N:\#\operatorname{supp}(z)\le k\}\), and \(\sigma_k(x)_X:=\inf_{z\in\Sigma_k}\|x-z\|_X\). In particular, determine when the minimal number of measurements \(n\) is of the same order as \(k\).
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2007/36](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1592), page 14. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Reproducing subgroups of the metaplectic–Heisenberg group
statement:
Determine which Lie subgroups $H$ of the semidirect-product group $G$ formed from the (double cover of the) symplectic group $Sp(d,\mathbb R)$ and the Heisenberg group $H_d$, modulo the irrelevant center, admit an analyzing window $\phi\in L^2(\mathbb R^d)$ such that, for every $f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d)$, the reproducing formula

$$f=\int_H\langle f,\mu_e(h)\phi\rangle\,\mu_e(h)\phi\,dh$$

holds in the weak sense, where $\mu_e$ is the extended metaplectic representation and $dh$ is Haar measure on $H$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2007/36](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1592), page 69. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Classification of central Frattini extensions by small group rings
statement:
Fix a finite $p$-group $H$, where $p$) is an arbitrary prime, and let $k=\mathbb F_p$. Let $\mathcal F(H)$ be the collection of short exact sequences of finite $p$-groups
\[
1\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow G\longrightarrow H\longrightarrow 1,
\]
where $A$ is elementary abelian, central in $G$, and contained in the Frattini subgroup $\Phi(G)$. Determine which sequences in $\mathcal F(H)$ yield isomorphic small group-ring sequences (equivalently, classify $\mathcal F(H)$ up to $s$-equivalence, and hence determine which central Frattini extensions of $H$ give isomorphic small group rings over $\mathbb F_p$).
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2007/55](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1738), page 7. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Embedding spanning subgraphs with a zero-free colouring
statement: For all $r,\Delta\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\gamma>0$, there exist constants $\beta>0$ and $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $n\ge n_0$ the following holds. Let $H$ be a graph with $\Delta(H)\le\Delta$ whose vertices are labelled $1,\ldots,n$ such that, with respect to this labelling, $H$ has bandwidth at most $\beta n$, has an $(r+1)$-colouring $\sigma:V(H)\to\{0,\ldots,r\}$ that is $(8r\beta n,4r\beta n)$-zero free, and uses colour $0$ for at most $\beta n$ vertices in total. Here an $(r+1)$-colouring is $(x,y)$-zero free if, for each $t\in[n]$, there exists $t'$ with $t\le t'\le t+x$ such that $\sigma(u)\ne0$ for all $u\in[t',t'+y]$. If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with minimum degree $\delta(G)\ge\left(\frac{r-1}{r}+\gamma\right)n$, then $G$ contains a copy of $H$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2008/01](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1782), page 58. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Strong coupling from a Stein coefficient
statement:
Suppose $W$ is a random variable with $\\mathbb{E}(W)=0$ and $\\mathbb{E}(W^2)<\\infty$. Let $T$ be another random variable, defined on the same probability space as $W$, such that, for every Lipschitz function $\\varphi$ (with derivative $\\varphi'$ defined almost everywhere),
$$
\\mathbb{E}\bigl(W\\varphi(W)\bigr)=\\mathbb{E}\bigl(\\varphi'(W)T\bigr).
$$
Suppose $|T|$ is almost surely bounded by a constant. Then, for any $\\sigma^2>0$, one can construct $Z\\sim N(0,\\sigma^2)$ on the same probability space such that, for every $\\theta\\in\\mathbb{R}$,
$$
\\mathbb{E}\\exp\bigl(\\theta|W-Z|\bigr)\\leq 2\\,\\mathbb{E}\\exp\left(\\frac{2\\theta^2(T-\\sigma^2)^2}{\\sigma^2}\right).
$$
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2008/25](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1970), page 42. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Maximum rank of real n × n × n tensors
statement: For a three-dimensional real tensor, rank one means that its entries have the form $a_{ijk}=x_i y_j z_k$, and the tensor rank is the least number of rank-one tensors whose sum is the given tensor. Question 3 asks: What is the largest rank of an $n\times n\times n$ real tensor? The report records bounds between $n^2/3$ and $n^2/2$ and states Conjecture 10, namely that the answer is $(1+o(1))\,n^2/2$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2008/44](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/2090), page 20. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Essential covers of the cube by hyperplanes
statement:
Cover the vertices of the discrete cube $\{0,1\}^n$ with as few affine hyperplanes $H_1,\ldots,H_k$ as possible, subject to:

1. Every $H_i$ is essential: for every $i$, there is a point in the cube that only $H_i$ covers.
2. Every variable appears somewhere: for every $n\ge j\ge 1$, there is an index $i$ such that the variable $x_j$ appears with a nonzero coefficient in the equation defining $H_i$.

If $f(n)$ is the smallest such $k$, determine $f(n)$. The report gives $n/2+1\ge f(n)\ge\Omega(\sqrt n)$ and asks whether this gap can be closed.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2008/44](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/2090), page 72. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Conjecture 2 on subtree descriptions of mixed-integer vertex-cover polyhedra
statement:
Let $G=(U\cup V,E)$ be a bipartite graph, let $I\subseteq U\cup V$, and let $b_{ij}\in\mathbb{Q}$ for each $ij\in E$. Define
\[
S(G,I)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{U\cup V}: x_i+x_j\ge b_{ij}\text{ for }ij\in E,\ x_i\in\mathbb{Z}\text{ for }i\in I\}.
\]
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be the family of subtrees $T$ of $G$ such that $I_T:=V(T)\cap I$ coincides with the set of leaves of $T$. Conjecture 2 asserts
\[
\operatorname{conv}(S(G,I))=\bigcap_{T\in\mathcal{T}}\operatorname{conv}(S(T,I_T)).
\]
Writing $k$ for the smallest positive integer such that $k b_{ij}\in\mathbb{Z}$ for every $ij\in E$, the report states that this conjecture is open for every $k\ge 3$; its validity for $k=2$ follows from a known facet characterization.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2008/51](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/2489), page 31. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Tree-routing property of the symmetric Virtual Private Network Design problem
statement: For every simple, undirected, connected graph $G=(V,E)$, nonnegative edge-cost vector $c\in\mathbb{R}_+^E$, and nonnegative integer maximum-cumulative-demand vector $b\in\mathbb{Z}_+^V$, let $W=\{v\in V:b_v>0\}$. A VPN consists of exactly one path $P_{uv}$ in $G$ for each unordered pair $\{u,v\}\subseteq W$ and an installed-capacity vector $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}_+^E$ sufficient to route every traffic matrix satisfying $\sum_{u\in W}d_{uv}\le b_v$ for each $v\in W$. The symmetric VPND objective is to minimize $\sum_{e\in E}c_e\gamma_e$. The conjecture was that every such instance has an optimal VPN whose support, equivalently the union of its selected paths, induces a tree in $G$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2008/51](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/2489), page 52. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Minimal reducing subspaces of a finite Blaschke-product multiplication operator
statement: Let $B$ be a finite Blaschke product with $n$ zeros, counting multiplicity, and let $M_B$ be the induced multiplication operator on the Bergman space $L^2_a(\[0m\mathbb D)$. The report states that the largest $C^*$-algebra in the commutant of $M_B$ is finite-dimensional, with dimension equal to the number of connected components of the “Riemann surface” of $B^{-1}\circ B$ over $\mathbb D$. For $n\le 8$, this number equals the number of non-trivial minimal reducing subspaces of $M_B$. The open problem is whether this equality remains true for arbitrary $n$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2009/20](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/3470), page 2. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Nikolski’s lemma connecting the Operator Corona Problem with analytic projections
statement:
Let \(\Omega\) be a domain in \(\mathbb{C}^n\) (in fact, one may let \(\Omega\) be a manifold). Let \(F\in H^\infty_{E^*\to E}(\Omega)\) satisfy
\[
F^*(z)F(z)\ge \delta^2 I,\qquad \forall z\in\Omega.
\]
Then \(F\) is left invertible in \(H^\infty_{E\to E^*}(\Omega)\)—that is, there exists \(G\in H^\infty_{E\to E^*}(\Omega)\) such that \(G(z)F(z)\equiv I\)—if and only if there exists a function \(P\in H^\infty_{E\to E}(\Omega)\) whose values are projections, not necessarily orthogonal, onto \(F(z)E\) for all \(z\in\Omega\). Moreover, if such an analytic projection \(P\) exists, one can find a left inverse \(G\in H^\infty_{E\to E^*}(\Omega)\) satisfying \(\|G\|_\infty\le \delta^{-1}\|P\|_\infty\).
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2009/20](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/3470), page 23. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Determining the rank of a specific elliptic curve with torsion subgroup \(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/8\mathbb{Z}\)
statement:
For \(\lambda=15/272\), determine the Mordell–Weil rank of the elliptic curve
\[
E_\lambda:\quad y^2=x(x^2+Ax+B),
\]
where
\[
A=(\lambda^2-1)^4-32\lambda^4,
\qquad
B=-16\lambda^4(\lambda^2+1)^2(\lambda^4-6\lambda^2+1).
\]
The report gives an upper bound of \(3\) and two independent points of infinite order, so the unresolved issue is whether \(\operatorname{rank}E_{15/272}(\mathbb{Q})=3\) or \(2\).
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2009/33](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4076), page 54. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.
